Customer Implementation Manager
 This role sits at the intersection of project management, healthcare operations, customer success, and deployment execution. Implementation Managers are responsible not only for getting Canopy installed, but for ensuring each customer is operationally ready, clinically prepared, technically stable, and demonstrating healthy early adoption before transitioning into long-term Customer Success.
 You will serve as the primary customer lead during implementation, managing multiple workstreams across large health systems and coordinating stakeholders spanning Clinical Operations, Security, IT, HR, Communications, Training, Facilities, and executive leadership.
 Before services begin, you will own the path to readiness: defining the implementation plan, driving customer deliverables, assessing workflows, helping determine the right program design, coordinating site walkthroughs and installations, and ensuring technical and operational dependencies are completed.
 After go-live, your responsibility continues through stabilization. You will use customer sentiment, adoption data, system stability, and infrastructure health to determine whether the program is operating as designed and intervene when it is not. The Implementation Manager remains accountable until the customer meets defined stabilization criteria and is ready for a structured handoff to Customer Success.
 Success in this role means delivering more than an on-time implementation. It means launching a healthy, adopted, sustainable program that customers trust and that creates the foundation for long-term value and expansion.
 About Canopy
 Canopy is committed to creating safer and more supportive environments for those on the front lines of care. Our mission is to help hospitals ensure that healthcare workers feel safe, appreciated, and empowered every day to deliver the highest quality of care.
 We develop and deploy critical safety technology, including our wearable duress system and Real-Time Location System (RTLS) portfolio, delivered as a comprehensive service to enterprise healthcare systems across the United States.
 Join our collaborative, mission-focused team and use your implementation expertise to make a real difference in the lives of those who care for others.
 Key Responsibilities
 Own the customer from kickoff through stabilization
 Be the primary customer lead from kickoff through stabilization. Build confidence and trust with our partners and our team.
 Run multiple complex healthcare implementations at once, with clear ownership of commitments, dependencies, risks, decisions and next steps.
 Build strong, trusted relationships with customer project leads, clinical leaders, security teams, IT partners, executives and other stakeholders.
 Plan and drive implementation readiness
 Create, coordinate and execute project plans using Canopy's implementation playbook and best practices.
 Set clear expectations with customers and internal teams on responsibilities, timelines, readiness requirements and success criteria.
 Assess current workflows and help decide the right program design for each site.
 Partner with clinical and security leaders to design alert and response workflows that fit how each unit actually works.
 Partner with clinical leaders to build unit-level adoption plans and train clinical champions before go-live.
 Lead complex healthcare deployments
 Own every phase of the implementation: kickoff, technical configuration, installation, clinician training and go-live.
 Coordinate site walkthroughs, hardware orders and delivery, and device installations with Canopy teams and the customer's IT, Security, Clinical, Facilities, HR, Communications/Training and executive stakeholders.
 Hold both Canopy and customer workstreams accountable for progress toward the agreed services start or go-live date.
 Identify and manage project risks and issues, build contingency plans, and escalate at the first sign of risk.
 Protect implementation quality
 Treat implementation quality gates as real decision points. Make sure gate requirements are met and documented, and recommend holding a phase or go-live when readiness criteria aren't met. At Canopy, a quality implementation beats a fast one.
 Own post-go-live stabilization
 Keep ownership of the customer after go-live until the site meets the defined stabilization exit criteria.
 Assess program health with both quantitative and qualitative information:
 Wear rate and badge use
 Accidental alert rates
 Alert activity and response
 Customer and end-user sentiment
 System, gateway and device health
 Training or adoption gaps
 Spot unhealthy trends early and use the Canopy stabilization playbook to step in. That can mean workflow changes, more training, re-engaging champions, fixing infrastructure, escalating technical issues, or bringing in leadership.
 Coordinate fixes across the customer and Canopy teams when adoption, infrastructure, workflow or system performance falls short.
 On a regular cadence, report health, risks, adoption metrics, time-to-value and ROI milestones to customer leadership and Canopy stakeholders, with clear next steps.
 Deliver a strong Customer Success handoff
 Work closely with the Customer Success Manager throughout the implementation so the transition feels seamless to the customer.
 Identify early champions, executive sponsors, expansion opportunities and risks that may shape the long-term relationship.
 Transition ownership only after the defined exit criteria are met. Document the handoff: customer goals, stakeholder relationships, implementation history, program design, health metrics, adoption trends, open risks, technical considerations and agreed next steps.
 Improve the implementation practice
 Share field feedback with Product and Engineering to improve the product and service delivery.
 Help keep improving IM templates, playbooks and tools.
 Required Qualifications
 5+ years in customer-facing implementation, deployment, onboarding, customer success, or consulting roles, with a track record of leading complex projects from start to finish.
 Experience leading cross-functional implementations involving clinical, IT, security, HR, and executive stakeholders.
 Experience in healthcare, medtech, or another regulated operational environment.

As our Product Operations Manager, you will report to the Head of Product Operations and play an important role in improving how our Product Development organization plans, collaborates, and delivers. Working closely with Product, Engineering, and Design teams, you will help strengthen roadmap planning and execution, advance Product Development Lifecycle (PDLC) practices, and drive meaningful operational improvements. You will bring a proactive, data-informed approach to identifying challenges, uncovering opportunities, and leading cross-functional initiatives that help teams make better decisions and operate more effectively. This is a hands-on role for an experienced Product Operations professional who enjoys solving operational challenges and helping teams deliver customer and business value.
 - This position will be hybrid based out of our Lehi, UT HQ (3x per week)
 - If outside of UT, periodic travel will be required to our Lehi, UT HQ.
 - Reports to: Head of Product Operations (US based)
WHAT YOU WILL OWN
 - Partner with Product and Engineering teams to strengthen quarterly roadmap planning, readiness, capacity visibility, and alignment on priorities.
 - Facilitate planning and execution across assigned teams, clarifying ownership, milestones, and dependencies while proactively addressing risks and blockers.
 - Independently lead assigned cross-functional initiatives, driving stakeholder alignment, accountability, and progress from planning through delivery.
 - Partner with Product and Engineering Managers to improve dependency management, delivery forecasting, and alignment between product priorities and engineering constraints.
 - Strengthen adoption of Product Development Lifecycle (PDLC) practices, standards, and ways of working to improve consistency and execution.
 - Support product release and launch coordination, ensuring cross-functional readiness, clear ownership, and alignment with business stakeholders.
 - Maintain and improve operational reporting and dashboards, translating performance data and stakeholder feedback into actionable insights and recommendations.
 - Identify and implement improvements to Product Development processes, operating rhythms, and tools that reduce friction and improve effectiveness.
 - Develop and refine Product Operations playbooks, templates, and best practices, providing practical guidance to support team adoption.opportunities for continuous improvement that strengthen Product Development effectiveness.
WHAT YOU WILL NEED TO ACCOMPLISH THE JOB
 - 3–5+ years of experience in Product Operations, Technical Program Management, Product Management, Engineering, or a related discipline within a SaaS or technology company.
 - Demonstrated experience supporting roadmap planning and execution across Product and Engineering teams, including prioritization, capacity planning, and dependency management.
 - Experience independently leading cross-functional product development initiatives, coordinating stakeholders, managing dependencies, and addressing execution risks.
 - Experience improving operational processes, frameworks, and ways of working within Product Development organizations.
 - Strong working knowledge of modern software development practices, methodologies, and lifecycles.
 - Technical fluency with product development tools such as Linear or Jira and analytics platforms, with an understanding of engineering and delivery metrics.
 - Strong analytical skills with experience developing operational reporting, interpreting performance data, and translating findings into actionable recommendations.
 - Strong business acumen with the ability to connect operational improvements to delivery effectiveness, customer value, and business outcomes.
 - Excellent communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build alignment across Product, Engineering, and business teams.
 - Demonstrated ability to work independently, navigate ambiguity, identify operational challenges, and drive practical improvements.
WHAT WILL MAKE US LOVE YOU
 - You are a self-starter who takes ownership of responsibilities and proactively addresses challenges.
 - You have firsthand experience working with Product and Engineering teams and understand the realities of software development and delivery.
 - You naturally identify gaps, connect information, and bring forward practical recommendations.
 - You build trusted relationships through collaboration, communication, and follow-through.
 - You balance operational structure with flexibility, improving how teams work without introducing unnecessary complexity.
 - You are analytical and curious, using data and feedback to identify opportunities others may miss.
 - You are highly organized and comfortable managing multiple priorities, stakeholders, and initiatives.
 - You are energized by solving operational challenges and helping teams work more effectively together.

jobs.description:
Remote role based in Athens, covering mostly US East Coast hours (afternoons and evenings in Athens). Independent contractor engagement at $3,500–$4,500 per month (USD), depending on experience. As a contractor, you’ll invoice us monthly and handle your own taxes and social security contributions.
ABOUT 3Y HEALTH
3Y Health is building the operating system for healthcare practices, an AI-native platform that helps clinicians start, run and grow their practice. We work as a managed services organization (MSO): along with the software, our operations team runs the back office for the clinics we partner with, including billing, insurance and compliance. We currently serve applied behavior analysis (ABA) therapy practices and are expanding into other specialties. We're backed by over $200mm from Founders Fund, General Catalyst, SoftBank and 8VC.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We enter new markets by acquiring a foundational clinic for each specialty and region we go into, and we partner with independent clinics across the country. Every clinic adds entities, filings, contracts, staff records and deadlines that need to stay in order.
In this role, you'll own a set of our entities from start to finish. When we acquire a clinic, you'll carry out its integration plan: collect and file the records, prepare the filings, get staff ready for day one and follow up with everyone until each item is closed. Each deal comes with a detailed plan and timeline from the deal lead. Acquired clinics keep running largely as they do today until we bring them onto our platform, usually within a few months. Once a clinic is integrated, you'll keep its entity in good standing, alongside the existing entities you own.
You don't need experience in US healthcare. Every deal comes with a detailed checklist, and we'll teach you the US specifics. You need to learn fast, care about details and follow through. You'll work closely with our Corporate Development, Legal, Billing and HR teams in the US, and with a teammate in the same role.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
Acquisitions
 - Work through each deal's integration checklist from before signing through the first months after close, keep the tracker current, and flag anything at risk of slipping
 - Document how the clinic runs today, such as scheduling, intake, referrals and billing handoffs
 - Check that each acquired entity is in good standing, and that its legal name and tax ID match across IRS, state, bank and payer records
 - Support our team and advisors on payer change-of-ownership notices, Medicare enrollment updates and credentialing checks
 - Map every payer's electronic payment setup (EFT/ERA) and each clinic's bank accounts, so our billing team can keep cash flowing through close
 - Prepare staff for day one: verify the employee roster, gather employment records for legal review, run license and exclusion checks, collect onboarding paperwork securely, and help get payroll, benefits and staff FAQs ready
 - Inventory each clinic's vendors, software and logins, collect business associate agreements (BAAs) for legal review, and track which systems switch to ours at close, later or not at all
 - Follow through after close on staff communication, moving patients of departing providers to remaining clinicians, lease and facility license items, and the former owners' transition commitments
Entity management and corporate operations
 - Keep the entities you own in good standing, primarily by managing our vendors: prepare annual reports, state registrations, IRS updates and other filings, and track them to on-time filing with our legal team
 - Maintain entity records, including formation documents, officers, registered agents and ownership
 - Prepare and submit provider and facility enrollments with state Medicaid programs and other public payers, and track them to approval
 - Make sure incoming mail for your entities is logged, routed and acted on, especially anything with a deadline
 - Prepare contracts from templates, route them for signature, and keep our contract management system and renewal dates current
 - Note what worked and what didn't, so our checklists get better with each deal
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
 - 2–5 years in healthcare operations, practice management, credentialing or provider enrollment, or acquisition integration
 - A track record of managing many details and deadlines to completion
 - Comfort working with contracts, licenses and government forms. You read carefully and catch errors.
 - Strong spreadsheet skills, and quick to learn new systems
 - Excellent written and spoken English. Most of your work is with US teams, agencies and vendors, and most decisions happen in writing.
 - Comfort handling confidential information
 - High agency and low ego. You don't need to be chased, and you'll do the tedious work as carefully as the interesting work.
 - Based in Athens and able to work mostly US East Coast hours (afternoons and evenings in Athens)
NICE TO HAVE
 - Experience in US healthcare, insurance or another regulated industry
 - Experience working with US companies or customers
 - Experience with corporate filings, contract administration or compliance work
 - Daily use of AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT to work faster
WHAT WE OFFER
 - A monthly fee of $3,500–$4,500 (USD), depending on experience
 - A long-term role at a venture-backed US company, working closely with leadership
 - Room to grow as we acquire more clinics and enter new specialties
ENGAGEMENT
This is a long-term independent contractor engagement with 3Y Health, not an employment contract. You'll need to be registered as a freelancer in Greece, or be willing to register before your start date. You'll be paid monthly in USD.
If you meet most of the requirements and the role interests you, we'd like to hear from you, even if you don't check every box.

 Facilities & Vendor Management 
 Act as the primary on-site owner for all office issues and manage resolutions from start to finish, whether it is a minor maintenance request or an urgent building system failure.
 Conduct daily walkthroughs to ensure the space remains pristine, functional, and safe by identifying maintenance needs and inventory shortages before they impact the team.

You will also partner with Sales, Finance and Legal on Professional Services contracts, as well as Product & Engineering, and Customer Support to manage dependencies, risks, reporting, change control, and successful transition to ongoing operations.

 Lead projects delivery across the Americas, ensuring consistent execution of customer onboarding and implementation projects. 
 Coach and support Project Managers to strengthen delivery discipline, accountability, and continuous improvement. 
 Own project execution governance from initiation through closure, delivering agreed outcomes on time and within budget. 
 Govern SOW execution, monitor scope adherence, and drive formal change control when required. 
 Coordinate planning, resource allocation, and cost estimation across cross-functional delivery teams. 
 Maintain portfolio-level reporting on project status, budget, risks, issues, and delivery forecasts. 
 Partner with PMO and Finance on time tracking, billing readiness, month-end invoicing, and financial hygiene. 
 Manage stakeholder communications, executive reporting, and escalations to protect delivery outcomes. 
 Ensure smooth handover of implemented solutions to Customer Support and business operations teams. 
 Advance PMO best practices through lessons learned, standardized delivery artifacts, and stronger governance.

 Projects delivered in line with SOW commitments, including scope, milestones, budget, and acceptance criteria.

 High customer satisfaction and successful onboarding against project objectives. 
 A high-performing project management team developed through coaching and continuous improvement.

 People management experience

About Us
 Fanatics is building a leading global digital sports platform. We ignite the passions of global sports fans and maximize the presence and reach for our hundreds of sports partners globally by offering products and services across Fanatics Commerce, Fanatics Collectibles, and Fanatics Betting & Gaming, allowing sports fans to Buy, Collect, and Bet. Through the Fanatics platform, sports fans can buy licensed fan gear, jerseys, lifestyle and streetwear products, headwear, and hardgoods; collect physical and digital trading cards, sports memorabilia, and other digital assets; and bet as the company builds its Sportsbook and iGaming platform. Our more than 22,000 employees are committed to relentlessly enhancing the fan experience and delighting sports fans globally. 
 Overview 
 Fanatics is looking for a Business Operations Associate to run the systems behind Fanatics ONE benefits and to make sure every dollar the program spends gets charged to the right budget.
 Fanatics ONE is the loyalty program that recognizes fans across the Fanatics ecosystem. Members earn gifts and access to events they can't buy anywhere else, from seats at sold-out games to Fanatics Fest.
 Every gift campaign and member event has a back office behind it. Someone has to price the tickets, code the expenses, track the invoices and bill other teams when they use what we've paid for. That work keeps growing as more of the company shares our tickets and events. Right now, that responsibility is spread across several people within their own functions, so this role brings it together in one place, with a view across the whole program.
 A big part of the job is TicketManager, the system where we hold tickets and suites for sports and concerts. Colleagues across Fanatics claim seats from it. We want to open more of that inventory to other teams so we can pool budgets and buy more, and that only works if every seat carries a real price and every claim gets billed to the team that used it.
 This is a systems role first and a finance role second. The person who does well here likes building and fixing the tools a team runs on, and has an eye to catch financial numbers that don’t add up.
 You'll report to the Senior Manager, Strategy & Partnerships and work closely with Gifting Operations, Event Production, Bespoke Benefits, Finance, and our analytics team.

 TicketManager and ticket inventory

 Manage day-to-day operations of Fanatics Fest ticketing
 Intake and systems

 Build automations and small tools that replace manual tracking
 Show teammates how to submit requests and expenses the right way

 Details matter to you. When you spot a miscoded expense or a mispriced seat, you fix it right away.
 You can look at a complicated process that runs across several teams and systems and work out how the pieces fit together.
 Building things is how you solve problems. If a task gets done by hand every week, you want to automate it, and you enjoy making the work easier for everyone around you.
 You work well with people on other teams, and you know how to ask a busy colleague for help in a way that's easy to say yes to.
 When something is waiting on someone else, you follow up until it's done.

 Strong spreadsheet skills in Excel or Google Sheets
 A working knowledge of budgets and basic accounting, or the ability to pick it up quickly

Accountabilities
 In this role, you will support the Sales and Business Management teams by coordinating daily operations, maintaining accurate information, and ensuring consistent follow-through on commercial activities. Your responsibilities will include:
 Partner with local Business Managers to maintain accurate account and client records and support the management of current and upcoming opportunities.
 Maintain and update Salesforce records, ensuring data accuracy and compliance with established sales processes and reporting standards.
 Assist with preparing client proposals, presentations, and quotations in accordance with quality standards.
 Manage client communications when Business Managers are unavailable, providing responsive, professional, and customer-focused support.
 Receive, qualify, and record incoming leads in the CRM, ensuring appropriate follow-up actions are assigned and completed.
 Identify potential leads through CRM databases and LinkedIn, helping Business Managers develop new client relationships and schedule meetings.
 Collect information and prepare sales reports and other requested CRM analyses.
 Coordinate with the Sales Team to ensure submissions meet deadlines and follow-up schedules are maintained.
 Track lost opportunities, maintain relevant records, and support investigations into the reasons behind unsuccessful opportunities.
 Contribute to marketing initiatives, including case studies, conferences, and brochures, in collaboration with Sales and Engineering teams.
 Review existing sales processes and recommend improvements or new procedures to address evolving business needs.
 Coordinate with estimation, project management, finance, and other departments to facilitate information sharing and ensure sales-related timelines are met.
 Requirements
 The ideal candidate is a detail-oriented and resourceful professional with a strong background in customer service, sales support, or sales operations. You should be comfortable managing multiple priorities, communicating with different stakeholders, and working in a technology-driven environment. The following qualifications are expected:
 Post-secondary education in a relevant field or equivalent professional experience.
 At least five years of experience in customer service, support, or a sales-focused position.
 Previous experience in the technology sector or within a professional services organization.
 Proficiency with Salesforce and CRM data management.
 Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Word, Excel, and Outlook.
 Familiarity with AI tools and a willingness to continuously develop new skills.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with fluency in English.
 Strong organizational and prioritization skills, combined with exceptional attention to detail.
 Ability to build positive working relationships with clients, colleagues, and cross-functional teams.
 Adaptability and confidence working in a changing, diverse, and collaborative environment.
 Ability to obtain the security clearance required under the Controlled Goods Program (CGP).
 Experience with the Controlled Goods Program, aerospace, or defense industries is considered an asset.

 This is a fully remote position.
 Occasional travel to Canadian offices may be required.
 The role involves access to export-controlled information governed by ITAR and EAR regulations. Candidates must qualify as a U.S. person under 22 CFR 120.62 or be eligible to obtain an export license.
 Candidates will be required to complete the applicable security screening.

 Annual profit-sharing bonus.
 Additional supplementary benefits.
